chunk_findings.detail: A clean worktree plus a transient `git stash list` failure after a no-op `git stash push` now makes `_stash_away` raise `RuntimeError`, even though the correct contract is to return `""` because there was no work. `git stash push -u -m tag` exits 0 with “No local changes to save”; if `git stash list` then fails three times, `_stash_find_sure` returns `None`, and the fallback only recognizes the new entry if `refs/stash`’s top subject contains this operation’s tag. With no existing stash (or an existing top stash without this tag), it raises. The old implementation returned `""` in this situation, so a no-change sync did not fail solely because the shared stash list was temporarily unreadable.

chunk_findings.detail: The new branch calls `why.startswith(DROP_INCOMPLETE)` without checking whether `_stash_back(tree, tag, sha)` returned `None`. chunk_findings.detail: The new no-op detection searches `git`'s human-readable output for `"no local changes"`. Since a successful `git stash push -u -m tag` prints `Saved working directory and index state On <branch>: tag`, any `tag` containing `"no local changes"` makes `_stash_away(tree, "no local changes")` return `""` even though a stash was actually created. The caller will proceed as if the tree was clean and never apply that stash, orphaning the user's work. The helper's contract places no restriction on `tag`, so this is a regression from the previous lookup-by-tag behavior.

chunk_findings.detail: The retry predicate checks the substring `"stash failed"` anywhere in `r.err`/`r.out`, not just Git’s specific transient `fatal: stash failed` diagnostic. Git error output can contain arbitrary user-controlled file paths. For example, a tracked file named `stash failed` that conflicts during `git merge --no-edit <source>` produces `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in stash failed`; this is misclassified as a transient stash failure, so the function sleeps and re-runs `git merge` while `MERGE_HEAD` already exists. The result returned is then the second invocation’s `fatal: You have not concluded your merge` instead of Git’s actual conflict details. Match only the dedicated `fatal: stash failed` line, not any occurrence of the words.

chunk_findings.detail: The test starts the lock-release timer before calling `W.merge`, but nothing guarantees `W.merge` reaches the first `git stash create` attempt before the held lock expires. Under a slow/loaded environment where `W.merge` spends more than 0.5s in setup before the first merge attempt, the lock is already gone, no `fatal: stash failed` occurs, and the merge succeeds on the first try; the test then passes even if `_merge_retrying_stash` has no retry logic at all. The 3s variant at line 55 has the same race. This makes the regression test nondeterministic and unable to distinguish a retried transient failure from a plain successful merge.

chunk_findings.detail: After `git stash push -u -m tag` succeeds with local changes, `_stash_away` treats any non-None `_stash_find_sure` result as authoritative. But `_stash_find_sure` returns `("", "")` whenever `git stash list` itself succeeds while the new entry is merely absent at that instant; that can happen in the shared-stash race this change is meant to handle. Concrete interleaving: session A pushes tagA and creates SHA_A. Session B is in `_drop` with a stale `stash@{n}` that now points at SHA_A; B runs `git stash drop` and gets SHA_A, but before B’s new `git stash store` puts it back, A runs `_stash_find_sure`: `git stash list` exits 0 and has no SHA_A, so `_stash_away` returns `""`. B then stores SHA_A back, but A already believes there was no local work and will not apply that stash after the sync; the user’s uncommitted work is left hidden in the stash. “List succeeded and no entry shown” is not proof that `git stash push` saved nothing, so the data-loss race remains open.

chunk_findings.detail: `why.startswith(DROP_INCOMPLETE)` runs before the old `if why` truthiness guard. `_stash_back` returns `None` on a successful restore (the old code used `if why` to skip the failure branch). On a normal `ddflow sync --keep-local` where the stash applies cleanly, `why` is `None`, so this line raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'`, turning a successful sync into a crash after the work was restored.

chunk_findings.detail: The test only asserts that `_drop` returns `DROP_INCOMPLETE` with `theirs[:12]` and `"stash store"` in the reason. It never verifies that the stranger's stash entry still exists after the failed `stash store`. An implementation could lose the stranger's entry and still return exactly that incomplete message containing the SHA; the regression would pass even though the data-loss bug this fix is supposed to prevent is still present. The test should also assert the entry remains in the stash list, e.g. `assert theirs[:12] in _stashes(wt)` or `_git(wt, "rev-parse", "stash@{0}") == theirs`.
